Tatsuya Ōmine.name: Tatsuya Ōmine
Tatsuya Ōmine.power: Immovable. Any force that hits him goes into him instead of moving him; he can release the stored force later through a strike, a stomp or a shove. Stored force shows as faint amber hairline cracks under his skin, like light through ice. He can bank about a day's ordinary jostling; past that it leaks out as tremors (rattling cups, cracked tiles), worse when he is emotional. A full release tears his muscles and leaves him bedridden for a day. Growth: learning to bleed it off on purpose (Gentle Hands), later redirecting a blow into the ground.
Tatsuya Ōmine.intro_line: Tatsuya Ōmine, 19: huge, cat-ear beanie, shy amber eyes, a hoodie two sizes too small.
Tatsuya Ōmine.visual: A 196 cm gentle giant of nineteen with a thick amber-brown undercut falling over droopy honey-amber eyes, a grey knitted cat-ear beanie, a slate-grey hoodie a size too small, a humming damping ball on a cord at his belt loop, and faint amber fault-line cracks glowing under the skin of his forearms.
Tatsuya Ōmine.personality: Gentle, earnest, conflict-averse, quietly funny. Cooks for people to feel useful. Terrified of being the reason someone gets hurt. Believes that if he is small and useful he is safe to keep around.

voice_card.style: Soft and slow, formal ("-san"), stacked apologies, trails off when embarrassed, never swears. Tic: "Ah, sorry, sorry." Catchphrase: "Did you eat?" When sincere he goes short and plain with no apologies at all, which is how you know he means it.

Tatsuya Ōmine.hook: Blew out a gym wall in the entrance exam. Gentle giant who apologizes constantly and cooks for the house.
Tatsuya Ōmine.hidden: At 12 he stood in front of a skidding delivery van to protect his sister Rin; the van folded around him. Three days later he coughed and the family ramen shop's front window exploded (his school counselor submitted his name to Chikara Academy after that). He has never released everything and does not know where his ceiling is; he came to learn control, not to be a hero. Personal ladder (not an arc thread): 1 the van story (Act 1), 2 the shop window (Act 2), 3 he has never released everything (Act 3).

Home Kushiro, Hokkaido; parents Kenta and Yumiko run Ōmine Ramen (12 seats); sisters Haru 16, Mei 12 (knitted his beanie), Rin 9. Second cook from age ten; sends ¥10,000 home a month from his scholarship. Up at 05:00 to cook breakfast; weekend shifts at Crepe Expectations (very good, very slow, kids love him); Cooking Club. Maple room: half-finished knitting basket, ramen-shop photo, cat calendar, reinforced bed frame. Loves shio ramen and his mother's butter corn; cannot eat spicy food; lo-fi rain sounds; knits tiny things (coasters, sweaters for Mio's tools); feeds the courtyard cats. Stressed by yelling, broken dishes, anyone hurt near him; angered only by someone hurting Mio or a child (goes completely silent). Newcomers: warm on sight, offers food; trust comes from being trusted near him (stand close in a fight, hand him something fragile). Romance: eligible, very slow and shy, never physical without explicit clarity. Gifts: loves cat things and letters with a photo; likes good knives, yarn, Hokkaido snacks; dislikes fragile things and gym gear. Divergence: ignored, he still leaves a plate out; befriended, he asks them to spar (his first ask); rival must prove they can take a real fight because he will not hit back.

Mio Tachibana.name: Mio Tachibana
Mio Tachibana.power: Exploded View. She hears metal as a hum and a chord. She can pull any machine or metal object apart into a floating exploded diagram, every part hovering in its place, then reassemble it as something else. Violet field lines and parts suspended in technical-drawing order; reassembly snaps together with copper sparks. Metal and machines only, range about 20 metres; stress scatters the parts dangerously; more than about three reassemblies in a fight brings nosebleeds. Growth: legitimate control gear (Built, Not Born) and working through the shake instead of hiding it.
Mio Tachibana.intro_line: Mio Tachibana, 18: tiny, violet-tipped bob, cracked goggles, screws orbiting her.
Mio Tachibana.visual: A tiny 151 cm young woman with a messy jaw-length black bob fading into electric-violet tips, big violet eyes ringed in copper over tired shadows, cracked copper-rimmed welding goggles pushed up on her head, an oversized gunmetal work jacket, a label maker on a carabiner, and screws orbiting her hand in violet field lines.
Mio Tachibana.personality: Brilliant, kind, jumpy, perfectionist. Over-explains when comfortable, goes quiet and deflects when cornered. Hates being thanked for the wrong thing. Believes that if she fixes everything, nobody will look at her.

voice_card.style: Fast and technical, run-on sentences that stall mid-thought. Lie tells: stutters on the first word of a lie and says "It's nothing, really." Catchphrase: "Can I fix it? I can fix it." Kansai mutter "aho" only at machines. When sincere she goes slow and looks you in the eye, which she never otherwise does.

Mio Tachibana.hook: Brilliant gear-builder who takes machines apart in the air. The loft bedroom doubles as her workshop; she is on a Support scholarship she cannot afford to lose.
Mio Tachibana.hidden: Borrowed ¥450,000 through Nightshade Exchange to buy a black-market control rig (a stabilizer bracelet). At the entrance exam her nerves broke and her parts scattered; the rig held her steady, so the result showed her real strength, faked steady, and she cheated to get it. With interest the debt stands at ¥720,000 by Day 60. The rig is hidden under the loose floorboard in Sakura Lane Sharehouse/loft-bedroom (her mother's photo is kept inside a radio case in the room). She also sends ¥30,000 home each month and her father does not know it comes from her. Full path in arc-bible.md.
Mio Tachibana.personal_quest: Built, Not Born (works even if the secret never comes out)

Home Higashiōsaka (small-factory town); father Gorō runs Tachibana Press, a three-machine metal-pressing workshop going under; her mother died when she was nine (at the funeral every screw in the temple chairs rose into the air); no siblings. Sleeps 02:00-07:00. Gearshift Support Shop Tue/Thu/Sat, paid in cash and parts; Support Engineering club. Loft: workbench, pegboard wall, soldering fumes, radio collection, the floorboard she will not step on. Melon soda, convenience-store onigiri, forgets meals; old shōwa radio; restores radios, names her tools (the drill press is Kevin). Stressed by her phone buzzing, anyone near the floorboard, praise; angered by Support work mocked as not real heroics; secretly makes bad puns. Newcomers: flees, then sends an over-detailed text from the loft; trust comes from bringing her something broken to fix and leaving her alone with it. Romance: eligible, slow and all subtext (she builds you something), but she pulls away until the secret is told. Gifts: loves a vintage radio, a quality screwdriver set, melon soda by the case; likes label tape, snacks; dislikes jewellery (reminds her of the bracelet) and anything with a camera. Divergence: ignored, she disappears for a week around Day 60; befriended, she shows the floorboard early; rival, she cracks and the rival becomes the person who pushed her into confessing. Secret ladder: 1 money trouble (Act 1), 2 criminal lender (Act 2), 3 Nightshade Exchange (Act 3), 4 the rig was a control stabilizer, real power faked steady (Act 3, gated).

Shin Asakura.name: Shin Asakura
Shin Asakura.power: Rewind. He touches a non-living thing and makes it replay its last few minutes backwards. That includes impacts: force that landed in the last few minutes, even on his own body, can be sent back the way it came. Pale grey afterimages of the object's past positions and a tape-rewind hiss. Only the last few minutes, one rewind at a time, never living bodies' movements, healing or death; pushing past about three minutes means a migraine and a nosebleed. He watches the rewind, which shows who handled the thing and how (only actions, no thoughts or labels).
Shin Asakura.intro_line: Shin Asakura, 19: white fringe over one eye, scarred brow, bomber jacket, hands hidden.
Shin Asakura.visual: A lean 178 cm young man with a white-bleached fringe swept over one eye above shaggy black hair, narrow grey eyes ringed in red, a scar through his left eyebrow, a black bomber jacket with a red lining, one wired earbud, a dented brass bicycle bell at his belt, and pale VHS-static afterimages flickering behind him.
Shin Asakura.personality: Guarded, observant, dryly funny, protective. Reads rooms before entering. Hates being managed. Believes nobody covers for anyone, you cover yourself.

voice_card.style: Terse, low, street-flat. Calls people by surname until he decides otherwise, then first names, which is a big deal. Tic: "...Sure." Catchphrase: "Means I'm watching." Casual, dry swearing. When sincere he says your first name and then nothing for a beat.

Shin Asakura.hook: Juvenile record as a gang lookout; distrusts staff; fiercely loyal to the house.
Shin Asakura.hidden: At 15 he was a lookout for the Nine Corners. When a friend, Daiki, was framed for a robbery, Shin rewound the evidence to clear him; Inspector Hirose of the Metropolitan Police saw what his power could do and pushed his academy application. The Nine Corners call it betrayal. Raised by his grandmother Fumiko, who runs a tobacco and lottery stand at the Kurokawa backstreet crossroads, which is also where the Nine Corners meet. Ladder: 1 record (Act 1), 2 the Nine Corners call him back (Act 2), 3 the lookout job at the backstreet crossroads (Act 2), 4 the job is a trap: the gang's revenge over Daiki (Act 2, inside Old Corners). In Act 3 his Rewind of Mio's envelope shows hurried, gloved handling and he must choose to cover for her or report it.
Shin Asakura.notes: 19; birthday 4 April. 178 cm, lean. Home the Kurokawa District backstreets; mother left, father unknown; poor, never asked anyone for anything. 4 a.m. walk, never sits with his back to the door; night shifts at Campus Corner Mart Wed/Fri; no club until Yūto drags him into Rooftop Wellness. Street room: window on the lane, bike-repair stand, shogi board, his grandmother's teacup. Cheap melon bread, canned black coffee; 90s hip hop on one earbud; fixes bicycles, phone shogi with his grandmother every Sunday night, bad action films. Stressed by cops, staff check-ins, unknown numbers; comforted by rooftops, his grandmother's voice, a bike chain clicking; angered by threats to Tatsuya or Mio or being called rehabilitated; cries over nothing on screen (one tear if his grandmother is hurt). Newcomers: watches without speaking and calls them new guy; trust from keeping a secret he tested them with, or covering for him unasked. Romance: eligible, slow burn through actions (fixes your bike, walks you home); being protected disarms him. Gifts: loves a bike part he needs, a shogi set, anything for his grandmother; likes melon bread, coffee; dislikes sentimental cards and anything with the academy logo. Divergence: ignored, he goes to the Nine Corners meeting alone and comes back hurt; befriended, he asks someone to come; rival he respects if they fight fair and despises if they use Standing as leverage.

Park Seo-yeon.name: Park Seo-yeon
Park Seo-yeon.power: Main Character. The more people watching her who want her to win, in person or live through a camera, the stronger, faster and luckier she gets. A golden backlight with lens flares and a translucent view counter shimmering at her shoulder; it feels like stage adrenaline. Hate-watching gives her nothing; alone in the dark she is an ordinary 19-year-old; a big surge ends in a crash (shaking, crying, 14 hours of sleep). Growth: a few people who truly believe in her, the house, count for more than millions.
Park Seo-yeon.intro_line: Park Seo-yeon "Sunny", 19, Korean: rose-gold waves, heart sunglasses, phone raised.
Park Seo-yeon.visual: A 165 cm Korean young woman of nineteen with voluminous rose-gold waves over hot-pink underlayers, sparkling pink-gold doe eyes, heart-shaped rose-gold sunglasses pushed up, a pin-covered customised blazer, a pink rhinestone phone in her hand, and a golden backlight with lens flares and a shimmering view counter at her shoulder.
Park Seo-yeon.personality: Sparkling, funny, performs confidence; underneath, tired and honest. Drops the act when someone sees through it kindly. Believes she is only real if she is watched.

voice_card.style: Bright, quick, camera-ready banter; Korean interjections ("aigoo", "omo", "daebak") sprinkled lightly; cute nicknames (bear for Tatsuya, gremlin for Mio, mafia boy for Shin). Tic: narrates herself to an imaginary camera when nervous. Catchphrase: "Hi hi!" When sincere, plain and quiet Busan dialect slips out with no nicknames.

Idol trainee in Seoul from 13, cut a month before debut at 16; her power woke on a live stream that night; two million followers by 18. Savings from brand deals, falling fast; refuses to ask her mother for money. Recruited into 1A on a Media scholarship; the scandal clip moved her to 2B. No job at first (later a Common Ground job); Arts & Media club, which she quits on Day 10 after Ayame's jab and rejoins in Act 4. Sunrise room: a dark ring light, a wall of old kind fan letters, skincare, horror DVDs under the bed, kimchi labelled in three languages. Convenience-store desserts and her mother's kimchi; K-pop she pretends to hate; astrology, horror films, editing videos she never posts. Stressed by comment sections, silence, her own unedited face; angered by anyone filming Mio or Tatsuya unasked; real laughter is a snort. Newcomers: a full charm offensive; trust from seeing her without makeup and acting like it is nothing. Romance: eligible, fast flirting and slow trust, never on camera. Gifts: loves a handwritten letter or an unposed candid; likes desserts, horror films, kimchi; dislikes anything branded or content gifts. Divergence: ignored, her power stays drained and she considers going back to Busan; befriended, a player becomes her first viewer (counts double); rival, she performs harder.

Kenji Arimura.power: Slipstream. He is fast, and everyone in his wake moves at his speed too (white wind trails and a contrail behind the group). Reiko Shimazu.power: Bastion. She draws a line and states a rule aloud, such as "no one who means harm crosses"; the narrower the rule, the stronger the barrier. A pale-blue hexagonal wall with the rule's words glowing in it. The barrier only stops what she worded: a loophole is a loophole.
